question: How many countries will ECDC's West Nile virus weekly report published around 30 October 2026 list as affected during the 2026 season?

calls.reasoning: The Week 42 report (data to 14 Oct) gives 19 countries / 222 areas. The count is cumulative, so 19 is the minimum. Two more reports (about 23 Oct and 30 Oct) come before resolution. Recent growth was fast (+3 countries in two weeks), partly from lagged reporting of northern spread (Belgium, Netherlands, Slovenia), and ECDC says more cases are expected. But the season is winding down and late-October first-time additions are rare. Türkiye has usually been in past ECDC lists but isn't among the 18 named countries in the Week 42 breakdown, so it is a plausible addition; other candidates are Slovakia, Czechia, Portugal, Bosnia and Montenegro. Market check: no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmaker market found.
sources: WebSearch summary of ECDC Week 42 Current situation (222 areas, 19 countries)
https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/documents/Communicable-disease-threats-report-week-37-2026.pdf (search snippet: 161 areas, 15 countries as of 10 Sep 2026)
calls.dossier:
- ECDC WNV weekly, Week 42 (data to 14 Oct 2026; via search summary of wnv-weekly.ecdc.europa.eu): 222 areas in 19 countries. Areas listed by country: Italy 70, France 28, Greece 25, Romania 24, Netherlands 15, Serbia 10, Belgium 6, Bulgaria 6, Croatia 6, Germany 6, Spain 6, North Macedonia 5, Hungary 4, Kosovo 4, Austria 3, Albania 2, Cyprus 1, Slovenia 1 (18 names in the snippet; the 19th, presumably Türkiye or another, was not visible). 1,926 locally acquired human cases.
- Trajectory of the country count: 15 countries/161 areas as of 10 Sep (CDTR wk37); 16/202 Week 40 (30 Sep); 18/208 Week 41 (7 Oct); 19/222 Week 42 (14 Oct). Slovenia appears new by Week 42; Belgium and Bulgaria were first-time additions around Weeks 40-41.
- ECDC press release, 15 Oct 2026: record season, 1,715 EU cases as of 7 Oct; virus circulating at lower levels as conditions become less favourable; 'additional cases are still expected' in coming weeks; spread north (Belgium's first local human cases, Netherlands 59 cases).
- AP/Yahoo, 15 Oct 2026: 18 countries, 1,855 cases, 141 deaths as of early October; 15 countries reported equine/bird outbreaks.
- Searched for first-time 2026 local cases in Slovakia, Czechia, Portugal, Türkiye, Montenegro, Bosnia, Switzerland, Luxembourg and Poland: nothing found. Poland had a probable local case in 2024. Türkiye usually appears in past ECDC lists but was not visible among the names.
- Status quo: the count stays at 19 (cumulative; cannot decrease).
- Reference class: in prior seasons (2018-2025), new countries in the second half of October are uncommon but do occur through delayed reporting. 2026 has been unusually fast late in the season (+3 countries between 30 Sep and 14 Oct).
- Resolves off the 'Current situation' sentence in the first ECDC weekly report published on or after 29 Oct 2026 (expected Fri 30 Oct, Week 44, data to ~28 Oct). Not news counts or EFSA/ECDC monthly reports.
- Event window: Week 42 baseline (14 Oct data) -> report of 30 Oct; as of 19 Oct, two weekly reports (about 23 Oct and 30 Oct) are still to come.
- Could not find: the Week 43 report (not yet published), the identity of the 19th country, any prediction market.

calls.reconciliation: All runs agree on the factual base: Week 42 = 19 countries, cumulative, two reports left, no market. The identity of the 19th country is not settled (Run 3 cites Moldova in the case list; Runs 1-2 guessed Türkiye). If it is Moldova, Türkiye remains a plausible late addition, which slightly supports upside. No web access on this run. The remaining disagreement, how likely 1-2 more additions are, is a judgment call. I weigh the 2026 record late-season pace and lagged reporting against waning transmission and land at roughly 50% stay at 19, 30% at 20, 13% at 21, 7% at 22+. I carry forward the runs' dispersion of ~2.
